These are different units from the 87 manuscript propositions.
execution_paragraph: Fresh verification passed 450 stages: 156 compilation targets, one exact-example execution, one axiom audit, 155 module kernel replays and 137 isolated rejection controls. The permitted logical axioms are propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Upstream libraries remain pinned dependencies and were not exhaustively rebuilt or replayed.

new_entries.title: Ideal statistical benefit of refinement
new_entries.guide_text: Actual nested conditional expectations yield the exact squared-risk decomposition. This concerns ideal predictors under a fixed distribution, rather than finite-sample fitting.

new_entries.title: Exact accounting for an enumerated grammar
new_entries.guide_text: Summable grammar evidence gives the exact posterior total-variation tail and predictive bounds. Exhaustive active sets converge inside the declared grammar.

new_entries.title: Prior-preserving program refinement
new_entries.guide_text: A whole-record likelihood mixture with split prior mass preserves evidence and posteriors. Prediction also requires the corresponding joint-likelihood mixture. Fresh duplicate prior mass changes the model.

new_entries.title: Missing-intervention nonidentifiability
new_entries.guide_text: The actual one-state instruments agree for every passive word but disagree under an omitted intervention. Complete passive laws cannot identify all actions.

new_entries.title: Reset-experiment probability certificate
new_entries.guide_text: Independent bounded reset trials yield simultaneous confidence and spectral table bounds. Experiment coverage is explicit, without independence between different words.

new_entries.title: Conditional observation-based stochastic completion
new_entries.guide_text: Population reconstruction, canonical cones and sampled spectral/operator estimates share one confidence event. Filtering retains state bounds, spectral separation and branch likelihood margins.

new_entries.title: Rational rotation and curved domain
new_entries.guide_text: The exact rational rotation has dimension three. Its unique closed convex invariant probability cone containing the initial state is the Lorentz cone, excluding finite normalized positive generators.

new_entries.title: Polyhedral approximation and law budget
new_entries.guide_text: Under the cosine bound, attenuation admits a regular-polygon certificate. The actual Lorentz base norm bounds error between full observation laws under a common policy.

new_entries.title: Sequential confidence accounting
new_entries.guide_text: Conditional coverage with a summable failure budget gives simultaneous coverage at selected or stopped stages. Robust acceptance retains initial-state coverage.

new_entries.title: Conditional learning with certified domains
new_entries.guide_text: Finite witnesses establish internal validity. Robust coverage and actual instrument discrepancies support per-horizon common-policy law bounds and conditional prediction.

new_entries.title: Matrix-embedding probability certificate
new_entries.guide_text: An actual injective symmetric matrix embedding and positive-definite interior derive a closed, pointed, generating PSD preimage cone, strict trace mass and compact normalized base. Literal nonnegative weighted congruences, including empty sums, give branch invariance, all-word probabilities and normalized observation trees under exact mass and initial coverage. Exact atlas transport retains the witnesses. The later ambient trace-norm paragraph is separate; no automatic norm equality is claimed.

new_entries.title: Exact rational matrix witness for the rotation model
new_entries.guide_text: The unchanged rational rotation model has the literal rational two-by-two embedding J, weight 1/5 W congruence, matrix-unit probe congruences and zero rotate branch. Derives injectivity, trace, PSD iff Lorentz, normalized disk, initial diag(1,0), definite interior and trace conservation. Every source word probability is unchanged. The P50 embedding retains P46's finite-positive-generator obstruction.

new_entries.title: Continuous-observation instrument semantics
new_entries.guide_text: Actual Bochner-integrable operator densities, whole-cone positivity outside a common null set and exact integrated mass construct Markov kernels and jointly measurable normalized updates with fixed valid fallback. Actual operator-product record measures are normalized and prefix-consistent under arbitrary measurable randomized history policies, with the proved kernel/update compProd bridge. Prescribed actions have the exact product-reference density. Positive normalized reference rescaling r mu with B/r preserves kernels, updates almost everywhere and full finite record laws.

new_entries.title: Polynomial Gram certificate for interval observations
new_entries.guide_text: Literal output/input Choi indexing and spectral factors derive positive congruence maps from PSD matrices. Actual interval power-stack Gram witnesses prove whole-interval positivity, including degree zero. Finite coefficient checks on a genuine basis imply full intertwining; actual uniform moments and Bochner integration check mass. The aggregate uses the actual P50 embedding/interior and constructs the P52 instrument, positive-density updates and all-horizon probability/consistency/product-density semantics. This is a sufficient certificate, not a completeness theorem.

new_entries.title: Conditional finite-moment identification
new_entries.guide_text: Genuine normalized uniform moments and positive squared integrals of nonzero polynomials derive Gram invertibility. A covered square population core in the supplied true dimension gives exact moment/coefficient reconstruction, the entire polynomial density and all word coordinates. Error uses one fixed induced norm. Actual bounded signed reset trials give the range-two simultaneous radius with positive counts, 0 < delta < 1, exact expectations and within-entry independence. Rank, degree, coverage and resets remain premises; event/table integral dictionaries are explicit.

new_entries.title: A valid continuous counterexample to finite-moment identification
new_entries.guide_text: Actual cubic Legendre densities 1 +/- epsilon L3 for 0 < epsilon < 1 are strictly positive and normalized with equal moments 0,1,2. Genuine integration gives integral |L3| = 13/40 and actual measure TV = 13epsilon/40, hence distinct laws. Independent finite product laws share every low-order product moment at all lengths. Actual scalar event realization and integral dictionaries give rank-one event Hankel matrices containing empty experiments. Nonzero perturbations are outside the quadratic class.

new_entries.title: Exact bin coarsening and its posterior
new_entries.guide_text: Literal Bochner cell operators preserve the cone and exact action mass. A finite measurable partition constructs a measurable bin map. Under every policy based on action/bin histories, the actual continuous record measure pushes forward exactly to the actual finite integrated-cell instrument law at every horizon; normalized initials give finite priors. The positive-cell posterior averages actual fine updates with density weights, including zero outputs. A valid 3u^2 instrument separates integration from point sampling. Within-cell-reactive policies are outside the exact coarsening claim.

new_entries.title: Averaged congruence and covariance
new_entries.guide_text: The integral covariance identity preserves positivity for positive semidefinite inputs. Affine and uniform-interval specializations retain their integrability and reference-measure assumptions.

new_entries.title: Positive cell-average approximation
new_entries.guide_text: Actual normalized Bochner cell averages on a finite measurable positive-mass partition preserve the original cone, exact integrated mass and every cell operator. The genuine induced probability-cone base norm gives the Lh resolution bound. Actual uniform equal-interval distance integrals give Lh/3. Null/empty conventions and required finite masses, metric and Lipschitz hypotheses remain explicit; a point sample is not substituted for an integral.

new_entries.title: Continuous-record total-variation bound
new_entries.guide_text: Actual time-dependent Bochner DensityInstrument families on a common finite-dimensional probability cone and probability reference, with finite actions and one common measurable randomized full-history policy, have actual finite record-law TV at most min(1,(e0+sum epsilon)/2). Integrated contraction is derived from positive decompositions, and TV from the signed-measure half-density identity; no branch-density lower margin is required. The optional conditional-event helper proves an eventwise 2TV/min-masses bound with both masses positive, not the stronger adjacent full conditional-law statement.

new_entries.title: Exact recognition of a fixed certified template
new_entries.guide_text: Literal fixed-template coefficient/mass matching is a finite real linear system. Fitted coefficient-word observability derives uniqueness among all linear matches, including singular competitors. An invertible match transports the actual matrix-domain polynomial Gram certificate with unchanged Gram data, exact mass and actual finite record laws. Fitted initial PSD and mass normalization remain a separate check. Observability neither supplies invertibility nor guarantees existence.

new_entries.title: Conditional continuous realization with a finite domain certificate
new_entries.guide_text: Actual supplied finite dimension and polynomial degree with an invertible complete population core derive inverse-moment fitted coefficients, full densities and word likelihoods. The independent P53 finite matrix/Gram/moment witness and transformed initial PSD/mass check for that same family yield actual all-horizon laws. Literal original/atlas event-law transport, a sufficient invertible P60 template constructor, complete signed synthesis with separate packet positivity, actual bin-policy pushforward, P58 Lh and Lh/3 resolution and P59 common-cone/reference/policy budgets are connected to the same fitted instrument. No dimension/degree discovery, empirical coverage or generating-process adequacy is inferred.

new_entries.title: Oriented quadratic probability certificate
new_entries.guide_text: Actual positive-definite metric and centered mass coordinates derive a genuine curved ProbabilityCone, including empty spatial dimension. Literal Q, PSD remainder and nonnegative multiplier plus both inverse-metric orientation inequalities imply cone preservation. Finite interval SOS/Gram/degree/coefficient and exact moment checks construct the actual uniform-reference polynomial DensityInstrument and arbitrary-policy probability laws, word densities and prefixes at every horizon. This is a sufficient replayable certificate, not a completeness result for search.

new_entries.title: Conditional operator-only ellipsoid discovery
new_entries.guide_text: The literal fitted polynomial ratio, its invertibility and mass row derive the affine block form and unique fixed center. An actual one-dimensional symmetric invariant-form subspace with a positive-definite member, and an actual rank-one fitted anchor with nonzero normalized displacement, derive the unique normalized positive metric. Complete P62 witnesses, exact mass and initial coverage for the same fitted family then yield actual all-horizon laws. Boundary placement remains a conditional proposal; failed discovery does not prove invalidity.

new_entries.title: Valid positive polynomial approximation
new_entries.guide_text: Literal Bernstein-Durrmeyer integral coefficients define cone-positive degree-at-most-n polynomial operators with exactly unchanged integrated mass. The actual doubly stochastic kernel has squared displacement 1/(3(n+2)); its actual joint-law variance inequality gives integrated genuine base-norm error L/sqrt(3(n+2)) under the stated induced-norm Lipschitz premise. Actual common-policy record laws obey min(1,TL/(2sqrt(3(n+2)))). No finite true-degree assumption is imposed; adjacent scalar examples are separate.

new_entries.title: Certified coefficient error and approximation bias
new_entries.guide_text: Actual fitted positive Bernstein coefficients with exact average mass define a genuine DensityInstrument and finite policy probability laws. Normalized-input genuine base-norm coefficient budgets integrate to their average; the finite-action maximum is added to the actual P64 L/sqrt(3(n+2)) approximation bias. A separately supplied actual correction discrepancy is added by a proved integral triangle inequality. Positivity and mass alone do not erase coefficient error.

new_entries.title: Time uniform predictable residual certificate
new_entries.register_text: Partial in the stated restricted sector.
new_entries.guide_text: Partial: natural-number tests on standard Borel sample spaces. The predictable residual bounds retain the recorded sample-space, indexing and interval-rescaling restrictions.

new_entries.title: Sequential evidence and lower error
new_entries.guide_text: For tests in [0,1], integral discrepancies lie below total variation. The lower error certificate assumes a simultaneous residual event, supplied by P66 only in its restricted sector.

guide_entries.label: P11, P23, P24
guide_entries.title: Ideal risk and grammar
guide_entries.guide_text: Nested expectations decompose ideal risk. Summable grammar evidence controls tails. Prior splitting preserves whole-record evidence; predictive consistency also needs the joint-likelihood mixture.

guide_entries.label: P31, P35, P37
guide_entries.title: Stochastic identification
guide_entries.guide_text: Passive laws can miss interventions. Independent reset trials give simultaneous bounds. Observable completion retains experiment coverage, spectral separation and filtering margins.

guide_entries.label: P46, P47, P48, P49
guide_entries.title: Curved rotation and learning
guide_entries.guide_text: The exact rotation requires a Lorentz cone; finite positive generators fail. Polygon approximation has a common-policy budget. Sequential learning retains conditional coverage, initial coverage and summable failures.

guide_entries.label: P50, P51
guide_entries.title: Matrix certificates
guide_entries.guide_text: Injective matrix embeddings and positive congruences certify laws with exact mass and initial coverage. The rotation has an exact witness. Predictive base norm need not equal ambient trace norm.

guide_entries.label: P52, P53
guide_entries.title: Continuous instruments
guide_entries.guide_text: Integrable positive operator densities and exact mass give consistent policy laws and positive-density updates. Reference changes preserve laws. Finite polynomial Gram identities certify the whole interval.

guide_entries.label: P54, P55
guide_entries.title: Moment identification
guide_entries.guide_text: Correct supplied dimension and degree, with an invertible covered core, enable reconstruction. Without the degree restriction, positive rank-one laws share low moments while differing in total variation.

guide_entries.label: P56, P57, P58
guide_entries.title: Cells and averaging
guide_entries.guide_text: Exact bin laws require bin-measurable policies. Positive-cell posteriors average density-weighted updates. Congruence averaging retains covariance. Positive cell averages have base-norm resolution Lh, sharpened to Lh/3 for equal uniform intervals.

guide_entries.label: P59, P60, P61
guide_entries.title: Comparison and realization
guide_entries.guide_text: Common-cone, common-reference models admit full record-law budgets under one common history policy. Observable invertible template matching transports certificates. Realization retains true dimension, degree, domain and initial-state checks.

guide_entries.label: P62, P63
guide_entries.title: Oriented curved certificates
guide_entries.guide_text: Quadratic Gram identities require mass orientation. Exact moments and initial coverage give all-horizon laws. Operator-only geometry discovery is a conditional proposal followed by full-family verification.

guide_entries.label: P64, P65
guide_entries.title: Positive polynomial approximation
guide_entries.guide_text: Actual integral coefficients preserve cone positivity and exact mass without a true-degree assumption. The stated Lipschitz bias, fitted coefficient error and later correction budgets remain separate.

guide_entries.label: P66, P68
guide_entries.title: Sequential residual evidence
guide_entries.guide_text: P66 remains partial for natural-number tests on standard Borel spaces, with recorded transport and rescaling restrictions. P68 gives lower discrepancy evidence conditional on the simultaneous residual event.
